items.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016
items.q: So when there was a Wayne Shorter album or something it could take two months to take out those strange chords.

ctx.x: Do you like the fact that everything is available to them through the internet and so forth?

Well I think — of course you can’t fight it, but when I learned jazz, as I said, I learned it from the records or by listening, or in some part by playing with people. So I have transcribed so many songs. In the group Nexus for example, I did the chords and the saxophone player did the melody. So when there was a Wayne Shorter album or something it could take two months to take out those strange chords. Now you’ve got it, you can pay for it, you’ve got it on the internet. So the situation is of course totally…
Right. Didn’t you write a book about playing by ear?
